about: Boku is a San Francisco-based mobile payments company that lets consumers pay for digital goods and services using their phone bill or local wallets, serving merchants such as Spotify, Netflix, Google and Apple. It operates a network linking merchants to mobile operators and alternative payment methods across more than 90 countries. It is listed on the London Stock Exchange AIM (BOKU), with annual revenue near US$100 million. It is a B2B payments brand, known in the industry but not by consumers.

Frontier Digital Ventures is a Kuala Lumpur-based, ASX-listed (FDV) investor and operator of online classifieds and marketplaces in emerging markets, including Zameen in Pakistan, Fincaraiz in Colombia, Pointer in South Africa, Infocasas in Uruguay and Fazwaz in Thailand. It takes stakes in property and automotive portals. The portal brands are well known in their markets, but the holding company is mainly known to investors.

Goldmoney is a Toronto-based precious metals financial services company that allows customers to buy, hold and trade physical gold, silver and other metals in vaults, and to use them for payments and savings. It also runs a bullion wholesale business (Goldmoney Wholesale), and is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (XAU). Founded by James Turk in 2001, it holds billions of dollars of metal for customers worldwide. Consumer visibility is niche, mostly among precious metals investors.

Raksul is a Tokyo online platform for business printing and logistics, best known for its Raksul print ordering service for business cards, flyers and packaging, plus the Hacobu freight management and Novasell advertising businesses. It serves small businesses and enterprises across Japan. Founded in 2009 and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (4384) since 2018, it has revenue of over 50 billion yen. It is a B2B brand with moderate recognition among Japanese small businesses.

Tongshifu is a Chinese company in Jiande, Zhejiang, categorised under e-commerce and handmade products. The input shows about CN 560 million of funding, last dated August 2018, and appears in a listed-company search. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Guestlogix was a Toronto-based travel commerce technology company that provided ancillary revenue software for airlines, cruise lines and travel brands, covering sales of insurance, hotels, ground transport and in-flight retail through airline websites and apps. It was listed on the TSX Venture Exchange before being acquired in 2018. Its ownership today should be checked. It was a B2B technology company with no consumer awareness, though airline passengers used its tools without knowing, and it has low sponsorship relevance.

MoneyOnMobile is a Mumbai-based mobile payments and financial services company that offered bill payments, recharges and cash services through retail agents and a mobile wallet in India. Previously Calpian, a Dallas company, it was listed in the United States and India. It targeted underbanked consumers and small retailers. Funding is shown at around $38 million. It operated as a niche fintech and had limited broader brand awareness.

Raycloud is a Hangzhou-based Chinese e-commerce software and services company, offering cloud tools such as order and warehouse management for merchants on Taobao and Tmall, plus data and marketing services. It was listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange and later became subject to Chinese regulatory and ownership attention. It is a B2B brand known among online merchants in China but with no international consumer awareness.

Fanli (Fanli.com) is a Chinese cash-back and shopping rebate platform based in Shanghai, founded in 2006, that earns commissions from online merchants such as Taobao, JD.com and Amazon and returns part of the commission to users who shop through its site and app. It filed for a US IPO in 2018. Its customers are millions of Chinese online shoppers, and merchants pay for traffic. It is a recognised consumer deals brand in China, with little international awareness.

Myplas.com is a Shanghai-based Chinese B2B e-commerce platform for plastics raw materials, based in Hongkou, connecting plastic resin producers and traders with buyers and offering transaction and supply chain services. It earns commission and trading margin. The input shows funding of about CN 170 million, last dated July 2018. It is a B2B online marketplace with very low consumer awareness, known mainly in the Chinese plastics trade.

Network International is a Dubai-headquartered payments company that provides card issuing and merchant acquiring services, processing and digital payments across the Middle East and Africa, with customers including banks and retailers. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange (NETW) in 2019 and was taken private by Brookfield Asset Management in 2024. It is a B2B payments brand, known by banks and merchants but not by the wider public.

Sailvan Network is a Shenzhen-based Chinese cross-border e-commerce company that sells consumer electronics and other goods to overseas buyers through online marketplaces and trading platforms. It operates in B2B and B2C e-commerce. The input shows funding of about $37 million, last dated August 2017. It is an export-focused firm with low consumer brand awareness among overseas shoppers; sales growth depends on third-party marketplace policies.

Pepkor is a Cape Town-based retail group, listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (PPH), formerly Steinhoff Africa Retail, operating discount fashion and household chains such as PEP, Ackermans, Legit, Tekkie Town and Style, and a financial services unit. It serves mass-market consumers in South Africa and other African countries and Europe, with thousands of stores. Its brands have very high consumer awareness among lower-income households in South Africa.

Africa's largest food retailer, operating supermarkets and hypermarkets under Shoprite, Checkers, Checkers Hyper, Usave and OK Furniture banners, plus liquor, pharmacy and convenience formats. It sells groceries, fresh food and household goods mainly to mass-market and middle-income shoppers in South Africa and, historically, other African countries, and also runs the Xtra Savings loyalty programme and money-transfer services. Headquartered in Brackenfell near Cape Town, it is listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (SHP) and has well over 2,800 outlets and around 150,000 staff. Very high consumer brand visibility across Southern Africa.

Wellness franchise operator offering cryotherapy, infrared sauna, red light therapy, IV drips, compression therapy and other recovery services under the Restore Hyper Wellness brand. Founded in 2015 in Austin, Texas, it sells memberships and sessions to health-conscious consumers, athletes and recovery seekers through more than 200 franchise locations in the US and Canada, mainly in affluent suburbs. Backed by venture and private equity investors, it earns franchise fees, royalties and company-owned studio sales. Growing consumer brand with retail footprint, and natural fit with sport-related partnerships.

Chinese content delivery network and internet infrastructure company that provided CDN, cloud and data centre services to media and enterprise customers, listed on Nasdaq (CCIH). It faced declining revenue and was later delisted. The record shows a Singapore address, probably reflecting a later corporate shift. B2B infrastructure brand known to internet companies, with no consumer recognition or public profile. Revenue shrank as larger cloud providers gained market share.

about: Website Pros is an Australian digital agency based in Carrum Downs, Victoria, building and hosting websites and e-commerce stores for small and medium businesses and providing related online marketing services such as SEO and search advertising. Customers are local Australian companies buying website design, hosting and ongoing marketing packages. I do not have reliable details on its size or ownership, so the description rests mainly on the Crunchbase categories of e-commerce and internet. Likely a small, private B2B services provider with local rather than national brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Controladora Comercial Mexicana was a Mexican retail group, one of the country's largest supermarket and department store operators, with the Comercial Mexicana, Mega, Bodega Comercial Mexicana, Sumesa and City Market banners, and restaurants (California). Customers were mass-market Mexican shoppers. It was sold to the Soriana group in 2015, after a derivatives crisis in 2008, and the brands were absorbed or rebranded. Once a household name in Mexico, no longer operating independently.

about: YOHO is a Chinese fashion e-commerce and media company, running the YOHO! Boys youth streetwear platform and magazine culture, selling sneakers and streetwear through the YOHO!BUY site, app and offline stores. Customers are young Chinese streetwear buyers. Based in Nanjing and part of the YOHO group, which has stores and a trendy media presence. Known among youth culture in China, with potential for brand activations. I cannot confirm its ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Busche Performance Group is a US vertically integrated metal casting and machining group serving automotive, truck and industrial customers, making iron and aluminium castings and finished components. Based in Southfield, Michigan, it is owned by private equity. B2B manufacturer with a Tier 1-type customer base and no consumer brand awareness. I cannot confirm site details. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Vincom Shopping Mall refers to the shopping centre business of Vingroup, now Vincom Retail, which is listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (VRE) and based in Hanoi. It owns and operates dozens of Vincom Centers, Vincom Plazas and Vincom Mega Malls across Vietnam, leasing space to fashion, food, entertainment and department store tenants such as cinemas and supermarkets. Revenue comes from rents, and the malls draw millions of visitors a year. A 300 million dollar investment dates from 2015. Consumer-facing property brand with very high visibility in Vietnamese cities.

Singapore internet portal company named 701Search, appearing under online portals in the input. The data available does not describe its offering, users or ownership. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: US discount variety retailer targeting tweens and teens with products priced mostly at five dollars and below, covering toys, tech accessories, snacks, beauty, party and room decor. It operates well over 1,800 stores in more than 40 states, with annual revenue of about 4 billion dollars, and is headquartered in Philadelphia, listed on Nasdaq as FIVE. Consumer-facing brand with strong awareness among US families.

about: Chinese SaaS company that provides e-commerce tools for merchants to run online stores, social commerce and retail operations through the Youzan platform. Tencent-backed and tied closely to WeChat mini-programs, it earns revenue from subscriptions and payment-related fees. Based in Hangzhou and listed in Hong Kong. B2B, with brand awareness among Chinese merchants.

about: Brazilian shopping centre operator formed by the 2021 merger of Aliansce and Sonae Sierra Brasil, owning and managing dozens of malls with millions of square metres of leasable area. Income is rent and fees from retailers. Based in Rio de Janeiro and listed on the B3 exchange. B2B landlord, though its malls are known to shoppers.

Chinese supermarket and convenience store operator, a unit of the state-owned Bailian Group, running hypermarkets, standard supermarkets and small convenience stores mainly in Shanghai and nearby provinces. Customers are urban household shoppers, and revenue comes from grocery and fresh food retail plus supplier fees. It operated several thousand outlets at its peak under the Lianhua and Quik names and was listed in both Shanghai and Hong Kong. It has struggled against online grocers and rivals, and has been consolidated into Bailian. Strong local brand in the Shanghai area but largely unknown elsewhere.

Axiologix Education is a company in Egg Harbor Township, New Jersey, whose industries in the input are internet, shopping and software, and which is listed. No products or scale are described. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Catalent was a Somerset, New Jersey (shown as Tampa, Florida) contract development and manufacturing organisation providing drug delivery technologies, softgel capsules, biologics and cell and gene therapy services to pharma and biotech firms, with revenue near $4 billion. Novo Holdings completed its acquisition of Catalent in December 2024 for about $16.5 billion, taking it private. B2B, no consumer brand.

Global diversified healthcare company, listed on the NYSE (ABT), selling medical devices (FreeStyle Libre glucose monitors, heart devices), diagnostics, nutrition (Similac, Ensure) and established pharmaceuticals in over 160 countries. Revenue about 42 billion dollars, around 114,000 employees, founded in 1888 and based in Abbott Park, Illinois. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and consumers. Well-known consumer health brand worldwide.

Biopharmaceutical company, listed on the NYSE (ABBV), headquartered in North Chicago, spun out of Abbott in 2013. Key products are Humira, Skyrizi and Rinvoq (immunology), Botox and Botox Cosmetic, and oncology drugs. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and patients via health systems. Revenue about 55 billion dollars with tens of thousands of employees. Well known in healthcare, and a visible consumer brand through Botox.

Anglo-Swedish pharmaceutical company, headquartered in Cambridge, UK, listed in London, Stockholm and on the NYSE (AZN). Develops oncology, cardiovascular, respiratory and rare-disease medicines, including Tagrisso, Farxiga and Imfinzi, and vaccines. Sells to health systems worldwide, with revenue about 54 billion dollars and roughly 90,000 employees. B2B pharma brand, but visible through sports sponsorship history and brand marketing.

German life science company based in Leverkusen, listed in Frankfurt, with pharmaceuticals (Xarelto, Eylea), crop science (Monsanto acquisition in 2018) and consumer health (Aspirin, Bepanthen). Founded in 1863, around 95,000 employees and revenue about 46 billion euros. Customers are farmers, patients, pharmacies and consumers. Very strong consumer and corporate brand; long-time sports sponsor, including Bayer 04 Leverkusen.

Biopharmaceutical company headquartered in New York, listed on the NYSE (BMY), developing medicines in oncology (Opdivo), immunology and cardiovascular (Eliquis), hematology and neuroscience, including after acquiring Celgene in 2019. Sells to hospitals and pharmacies. Revenue about 46 billion dollars with 34,000 employees. Well-known pharma brand to healthcare professionals, less so to consumers.

The largest US for-profit hospital operator, headquartered in Nashville and listed on the NYSE (HCA), running about 190 hospitals and over 2,400 care sites in 20 states and the UK. Revenue about 70 billion dollars, around 320,000 employees. Customers are patients and insurers. Founded in 1968. Consumer healthcare brand with strong local recognition, B2B for the group name.

French global pharmaceutical group in Paris, listed on Euronext (SAN) and NASDAQ, with immunology (Dupixent), vaccines (flu and others), rare diseases and consumer healthcare (Opella, partially sold in 2025). Revenue about 43 billion euros, around 82,000 employees. Customers include hospitals, governments and pharmacies. Well known to healthcare professionals, and a visible brand in Europe.

Waltham, Massachusetts-based life sciences company, listed on the NYSE (TMO), supplying lab instruments, reagents, consumables, diagnostics and clinical research services to pharma, biotech, hospitals and academic labs. Brands include Fisher Scientific, Applied Biosystems and Invitrogen. Revenue about 43 billion dollars with around 125,000 employees. B2B scientific brand, famous within labs, little consumer awareness.

San Rafael, California-based biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (BMRN), developing therapies for rare genetic diseases, including Vimizim, Naglazyme, Brineura, Palynziq and Voxzogo for achondroplasia. Founded in 1997, it sells to specialist hospitals and patients and also markets the gene therapy Roctavian for hemophilia A. Revenue around 3 billion dollars. B2B and specialist healthcare brand, known to rare disease communities.

Palo Alto-based biotechnology company, listed on Nasdaq (BBIO), founded by Neil Kumar in 2015, developing genetic disease therapies through a hub-and-spoke model of subsidiaries. A heart-disease drug (Attruby, acoramidis) for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy was approved in 2024, with Bayer partnering in Europe, and infigratinib for achondroplasia is in late-stage trials. Revenue from product sales and licensing. B2B and clinical brand, known to investors and specialists.

South San Francisco-based biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (CYTK), founded in 1997 and developing muscle-targeted heart medicines; its first drug, Myqorzo (aficamten), was approved for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. It also has omecamtiv mecarbil for heart failure and further cardiac muscle programs, with partners including Sanofi in China and Japan. B2B pharma brand, known to cardiologists and investors.

Washington DC-headquartered science and technology conglomerate, listed on the NYSE (DHR), owning life sciences brands (Beckman Coulter, Cytiva, Leica, Pall, SCIEX, Abcam, Aldevron), and diagnostics (Cepheid). Founded in 1984 by the Rales brothers, it spun off Fortive in 2016, Envista in 2019 and Veralto in 2023. Revenue about 24 billion dollars, around 63,000 employees. B2B brand known in labs and industry.

Foster City, California biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (GILD), a leader in HIV (Biktarvy), hepatitis C and B, oncology (Trodelvy, Yescarta from Kite) and COVID antiviral Veklury. Revenue about 29 billion dollars with 17,000+ employees. Founded in 1987. Strong in HIV prevention marketing, a B2B pharma brand with some consumer awareness.

British pharmaceutical and vaccines group in London, listed on the LSE and NYSE (GSK), with vaccines (Shingrix, Arexvy), HIV medicines (ViiV Healthcare) and specialty medicines. Consumer healthcare split out as Haleon in 2022. Revenue about 31 billion pounds with about 70,000 employees. Founded in 1715 via predecessors. Strong brand in healthcare, with sports sponsorship history.

San Diego-based biotechnology company, listed on Nasdaq (HALO), whose ENHANZE drug-delivery technology enables subcutaneous administration of biologics licensed to partners such as Roche, Takeda and Bristol. Products using it include Phesgo, Darzalex Faspro and Opdivo Qvantig, and Halozyme earns royalties on partner sales. Revenue from royalties, around 1 billion dollars. B2B pharma technology brand.

Swiss biopharmaceutical company in Allschwil, near Basel, listed on SIX (IDIA), founded in 2017 as a spin-out from Actelion. Developing and selling cardiovascular and sleep medicines such as Quviviq. Revenue from product sales, with financial restructuring in recent years. B2B pharma brand, known to physicians.

Durham, North Carolina-based provider of clinical research, healthcare data and analytics to pharma companies, listed on the NYSE (IQV), formed by merger of Quintiles and IMS Health in 2016. Pharma, biotech and medical device clients outsource trials to it and buy prescription and market data from it. Revenue about 15 billion dollars with around 88,000 employees. B2B healthcare data brand.

Cambridge, Massachusetts-based biotechnology company, listed on Nasdaq (MRNA), a pioneer of mRNA medicines, maker of the Spikevax COVID-19 vaccine and the RSV vaccine mRESVIA. Founded in 2010. Revenue fell after the pandemic, and the company has cut costs. Strong brand recognition from the COVID vaccine.

Swiss pharmaceutical group in Basel, listed on SIX (NOVN) and NYSE (NVS), focused on innovative medicines after spinning off Sandoz in 2023 and previously the Alcon eye care business. Products include Entresto, Cosentyx, Kisqali and Leqvio. Revenue about 50 billion dollars with around 76,000 employees. Strong corporate brand, an active sponsor of sports and culture.

Gaithersburg, Maryland-based vaccine developer, listed on Nasdaq (NVAX), maker of the protein-based Nuvaxovid COVID vaccine and a vaccine technology licensed to Sanofi. Its Matrix-M adjuvant is the core technology, and Sanofi paid an upfront sum under a 2024 deal to commercialise Nuvaxovid. Founded in 1987. Revenue from partnerships and sales. Brand known mainly from the COVID pandemic.

Secaucus, New Jersey-based clinical laboratory company, listed on the NYSE (DGX), one of the largest US providers of diagnostic testing and health information services for patients, doctors and employers. Spun out of Corning in 1996, it runs patient service centres and hospital lab partnerships and competes with Labcorp. Revenue about 9 billion dollars. Strong consumer-health brand in the US.

Redwood City-based clinical-stage oncology company, listed on Nasdaq (RVMD), developing RAS inhibitors for pancreatic and lung cancer. Its lead drug, daraxonrasib (RMC-6236), targets multiple RAS mutations, backed by programs against specific mutants such as G12C and G12D. Founded in 2014 and led by Mark Goldsmith. Pre-revenue. B2B biotech brand, known to investors and oncologists.

Basel-based generic and biosimilar medicines company, spun off from Novartis in 2023 and listed on SIX Swiss Exchange (SDZ). Sells off-patent medicines in over 100 countries to hospitals and pharmacies. Revenue about 10 billion dollars with around 23,000 employees. Well-known pharma brand, active in sports sponsorship.

Gottingen-based life science equipment company listed in Frankfurt (SRT3), supplying bioprocess technologies for biopharmaceutical production, plus lab products (Sartorius Lab). Founded in 1870 and controlled by the Sartorius family, it majority-owns Sartorius Stedim Biotech in Paris. Sells to biotech and pharma makers, competing with Danaher's Cytiva. Revenue around 3 billion euros. B2B brand.

Miami-based clinical-stage biotech company, listed on Nasdaq (SMMT), developing ivonescimab, a PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody for cancer, licensed from Akeso. Led by Robert Duggan and Maky Zanganeh, it paid Akeso an upfront sum in 2022 for rights outside China and some other regions and is running lung cancer trials. Pre-revenue. B2B pharma brand known to investors.

Dallas-based healthcare services company, listed on the NYSE (THC), operating acute care hospitals and ambulatory surgery centers (USPI) across the US, with revenue of about 20 billion dollars. The USPI unit is among the largest surgery center operators, and Conifer provides revenue cycle services. Founded in 1967 as National Medical Enterprises. Customers are patients and insurers. Regional hospital brand.

San Carlos, California-based vaccine company, listed on Nasdaq (PCVX), developing next-generation pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (VAX-31). Founded in 2013, it uses a cell-free protein synthesis platform licensed from Sutro Biopharma and competes with Pfizer's Prevnar and Merck's Capvaxive. Pre-revenue. B2B biotech brand. Its earlier VAX-24 candidate showed strong adult data, and the company has no marketed product yet.

Boston-based biotech, listed on Nasdaq (VRTX), best known for cystic fibrosis medicines (Trikafta) and expanding into pain (Journavx), sickle cell (Casgevy, with CRISPR Therapeutics) and kidney disease. Founded in 1989, it sells to specialist hospitals and clinics worldwide. Revenue about 11 billion dollars. B2B pharma brand with strong patient community recognition.

Perrigo is an Irish-domiciled (Dublin) consumer self-care company with major US operations, listed on the NYSE (PRGO), making store-brand over-the-counter medicines, infant formula and personal care products for retailers, plus brands such as Opill, Compeed, Nasonex, and Good Start. Revenue is around $4.3 billion. Strong private-label presence in the US, with modest branded visibility.

Pfizer is one of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies, headquartered in New York, and best known for the Comirnaty Covid-19 vaccine (with BioNTech), Prevnar, Eliquis, Ibrance and Lipitor heritage. It sells prescription medicines and vaccines to health systems and governments worldwide, with revenue of roughly $60 billion and about 80,000 staff. Founded in 1849, listed on the NYSE (PFE). Very high consumer awareness, with a history of sports partnerships in some markets.

Alnylam Pharmaceuticals is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company that pioneered RNA interference (RNAi) therapeutics. Its approved medicines include Onpattro, Amvuttra, Givlaari and Oxlumo, treating rare genetic and cardiometabolic diseases, and it partners with Novartis on Leqvio. Customers are patients, via hospitals and specialty pharmacies. Revenue is growing past $2 billion, and it is listed on Nasdaq (ALNY). Known in healthcare, not to the general public.

Bausch Health is a Laval, Quebec based pharmaceutical and medical device group, with the Salix gastroenterology business, Solta Medical aesthetics and the majority of Bausch + Lomb, the eye health company. It sells prescription drugs, contact lenses and eye care products worldwide. Formerly Valeant Pharmaceuticals, with heavy debt, and listed on the NYSE and TSX (BHC). Bausch + Lomb has strong consumer awareness.

Genetix Biotherapeutics is a Somerville, Massachusetts gene therapy company, the renamed bluebird bio after its 2025 takeover by Carlyle and SK Capital. It develops and delivers approved one-time gene therapies for severe genetic diseases such as sickle cell disease (Lyfgenia), beta-thalassemia (Zynteglo) and cerebral adrenoleukodystrophy. Customers are specialist treatment centres and patients. Niche healthcare brand with low general awareness.

about: Hologic is a Marlborough, Massachusetts medical technology company known for women's health, with products in breast imaging (3D mammography), molecular diagnostics, surgical devices and Covid-19 testing. It sells to hospitals and labs globally, with revenue of about $4 billion. It was listed on Nasdaq (HOLX), and in 2025 agreed to be taken private by Blackstone and TPG in a deal valued at about $18 billion. B2B health brand with little general awareness.

Insmed is a Bridgewater, New Jersey biopharmaceutical company focused on rare lung disease, with Arikayce for refractory lung infection and, since 2025, Brinsupri (brensocatib) for non-cystic fibrosis bronchiectasis. It sells to specialist physicians and patients, and is listed on Nasdaq (INSM) with a market value of tens of billions of dollars. Healthcare brand with low consumer awareness.

about: QuidelOrtho is a San Diego diagnostics company formed in 2022 from the merger of Quidel and Ortho Clinical Diagnostics. It sells rapid tests (Sofia, QuickVue, Covid and flu tests), lab immunoassay and blood-typing systems to hospitals, labs and clinics, with revenue of about $3 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (QDEL). B2B healthcare brand, with some consumer awareness of its rapid tests.

Rite Aid was a Philadelphia-area US pharmacy chain with thousands of drugstores selling prescriptions, health products and groceries, plus pharmacy benefit services. It filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023, emerged in 2024 and filed again in 2025, closing or selling all remaining stores. Founded in 1962. Formerly a high-awareness US consumer brand, but now effectively wound down.

Royalty Pharma is a New York based buyer of biopharmaceutical royalties, funding and acquiring interests in marketed and late-stage medicines, such as Vertex's cystic fibrosis drugs, Biogen's Tysabri and others. It earns a share of drug sales without running labs. Founded in 1996, it is listed on Nasdaq (RPRX), with revenue of about $2.3 billion. B2B finance brand with little public awareness.

Sarepta Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company focused on genetic medicines for rare diseases, especially Duchenne muscular dystrophy, with the Exondys 51 and Vyondys 53 treatments and the Elevidys gene therapy. It is listed on Nasdaq (SRPT) and has revenue of about $2 billion, with Elevidys safety issues and restrictions in 2025. B2B healthcare brand with low consumer awareness.

Shields Health Solutions is a Stoughton, Massachusetts specialty pharmacy services company that partners with hospitals and health systems to run their specialty pharmacies for complex conditions such as cancer. It earns fees and pharmacy margins, with partners across the US. Founded in 2014, it received investment from Centerbridge and others, and Walgreens held a stake. Healthcare B2B brand with minimal public awareness.

about: Zoetis is the world's largest animal health company, headquartered in Parsippany, New Jersey and spun out of Pfizer in 2013. It sells medicines, vaccines, diagnostics and genetic tests for pets and livestock, including Simparica Trio, Apoquel and Cytopoint, in more than 100 countries, with revenue of about $9 billion. Listed on the NYSE (ZTS). Vets and pet owners know its products, though the corporate brand is B2B.

ICON plc is an Irish-headquartered global clinical research organisation (CRO), based in Dublin, providing outsourced drug development, clinical trial and commercialisation services to pharmaceutical, biotech and medical device companies, with about 40,000 employees across nearly 100 locations and revenue of roughly 8 billion dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (ICLR). It acquired PRA Health Sciences in 2021. B2B healthcare services brand with limited consumer awareness, though known in life-sciences circles.

Jazz Pharmaceuticals is an Irish-domiciled specialty biopharmaceutical company, with its headquarters in Dublin and major operations in Palo Alto and Philadelphia. It sells sleep and oncology medicines including Xywav, Xyrem, Epidiolex, Zepzelca and Rylaze, after acquiring GW Pharmaceuticals in 2021, and Chimerix in 2025. Customers are prescribers, hospitals and health systems, and annual revenue is around 4 billion dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (JAZZ). Pharma brand with little consumer awareness, as prescription drug marketing is restricted.

Teva Pharmaceutical Industries is an Israeli multinational pharmaceutical company based in Tel Aviv and one of the world's largest generic medicine makers. It also sells branded drugs such as Austedo, Ajovy and Uzedy, plus over-the-counter products, with revenue of roughly 16 billion dollars and operations in about 60 countries. Customers are pharmacies, wholesalers, hospitals and health systems. It is listed on the NYSE (TEVA) and Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. Known pharma name, with some corporate sports sponsorship history in Israel.

Abivax is a French clinical-stage biotechnology company in Paris, developing oral drugs that modulate the body's natural immune response. Its lead candidate obefazimod (ABX464) is in late-stage trials for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease. With no marketed product, revenue is mostly research funding and capital raised, and it has raised over 2 billion dollars in total, with notable funding in 2025. It is listed on Euronext Paris (ABVX) and Nasdaq (ABVX). Research-stage biotech with no consumer brand.

Angelini Pharma is the pharmaceutical division of Angelini Industries, an Italian family-owned group based in Rome. It sells prescription medicines in neuroscience and psychiatry, plus consumer health brands including Tachipirina (paracetamol), Moment, Tantum Verde and Angelini's Amuchina disinfectant range, in Italy and more than 20 other countries, and acquired Arvelle Therapeutics in 2021. Revenue is around 2 billion euros. Privately held and unlisted. Strong consumer health brands in Italy, and Angelini is known for sponsoring sport and culture locally.

Apogee Therapeutics is a San Francisco-area clinical-stage biotechnology company developing long-acting biologic antibodies for immunology and inflammatory diseases, including APG777 for atopic dermatitis, plus programmes for asthma and COPD. It has no approved products, so revenue is non-existent, funded by capital markets, with total raised around 2.6 billion dollars. It was founded in 2022 and listed on Nasdaq (APGE) in 2023. Research-stage drug developer with no consumer brand.

Arcus Biosciences is a Hayward, California biopharmaceutical company developing cancer immunotherapies, including the TIGIT antibody domvanalimab and the HIF-2a inhibitor casdatifan, with partner Gilead Sciences (which has large option rights) and Taiho. It has no commercial product and earns collaboration revenue. Funding raised is about 1.8 billion dollars. Founded in 2015, it is listed on Nasdaq (RCUS). Research-stage biotech with no consumer brand.

Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals is a Pasadena, California biotechnology company developing RNA interference (RNAi) medicines. Its Plozasiran (Redemplo) was approved for familial chylomicronemia syndrome in 2025, and other candidates target liver, obesity and lung disease, with partners including Sarepta, Novartis, Amgen and GSK. Revenue is from licence and collaboration payments. Raised nearly 2.5 billion dollars, it is listed on Nasdaq (ARWR). Biotech with no consumer brand.

Celldex Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company with headquarters in Hampton, New Jersey, and labs in Needham, Massachusetts. Its lead candidate barzolvolimab, an antibody targeting KIT, is in phase 3 trials for chronic urticaria and in other skin diseases. It has no marketed products, funding from share offerings of about 1.9 billion dollars, and it is listed on Nasdaq (CLDX). Drug-development company with no consumer brand.

Crinetics Pharmaceuticals is a San Diego biopharmaceutical company focused on endocrine diseases and endocrine-related tumours. Its first approved drug is Palsonify (paltusotine), an oral treatment for acromegaly, approved in the US in 2025, with candidates for Cushing's disease, congenital adrenal hyperplasia and carcinoid syndrome. It is moving from development to selling. About 2 billion dollars raised, and it is listed on Nasdaq (CRNX). Pharma brand with little consumer awareness.

Disc Medicine is a Watertown, Massachusetts clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing treatments for serious haematologic diseases. Its lead candidate bitopertin targets erythropoietic protoporphyria, a rare light-sensitivity disorder, and it also develops treatments for anaemia in myelofibrosis and chronic kidney disease. It has no marketed products and has raised about 1.7 billion dollars from investors and share offerings. Founded in 2017, it is listed on Nasdaq (IRON). Research-stage drug developer with no consumer brand, so a sponsorship fit would be hard to justify.

DRI Healthcare Trust is a Toronto-based closed-end trust, listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (DHT.UN), that acquires pharmaceutical royalties and receives income from streams on approved drugs, such as Entyvio and Keytruda-related products, for unitholders seeking healthcare exposure. Its managers are DRI Capital, a specialist in healthcare royalties. Revenue is royalty income from drug sales by pharmaceutical firms. Finance-oriented vehicle with a low public profile, and no consumer brand.

Dyne Therapeutics is a Waltham, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotech developing targeted therapies for genetically driven neuromuscular diseases, using its FORCE platform to deliver oligonucleotides into muscle. Its main programmes are DYNE-251 for Duchenne muscular dystrophy and DYNE-101 for myotonic dystrophy. It has no marketed products and has raised about 2.3 billion dollars. Founded in 2018, it is listed on Nasdaq (DYN). Research-stage biotech, no consumer brand.

Freenome is a US biotechnology company in Brisbane (South San Francisco area), California, developing multiomics blood tests for early cancer detection using machine learning, with a colorectal cancer screening test under FDA review and licensed to Exact Sciences in 2025. Customers are health systems and screening programmes, and revenue is from partnership payments. It has raised about 1.8 billion dollars. B2B diagnostics brand with limited consumer awareness. It announced a plan to go public via a SPAC in 2025.

Illumina is a San Diego company and the global leader in DNA sequencing and array technology. It sells sequencers (NovaSeq, NextSeq, MiSeq), reagents and software used by research labs, hospitals, pharma companies and population genomics programmes, earning about 4 billion dollars a year, mostly from consumables. It spun out Grail in 2024 after a failed attempt to acquire it. Listed on Nasdaq (ILMN). Well known in life sciences, but not among consumers.

Intellia Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage genome-editing company using CRISPR/Cas9 to develop in vivo and ex vivo therapies. Its lead programmes, with Regeneron, include NTLA-2001 for transthyretin amyloidosis and NTLA-2002 for hereditary angioedema. It has no commercial product and earns collaboration income, with about 1.8 billion dollars raised. Founded in 2014, it is listed on Nasdaq (NTLA). Biotech with no consumer brand.

Ligand Pharmaceuticals is a Jupiter, Florida biopharmaceutical company that licenses and earns royalties on drugs developed with its technologies, including Captisol-enabled medicines such as Kyprolis, Evomela and Nexterone, and royalties on Promacta, with antibody discovery platform OmniAb spun out in 2022. It has a small team and a royalty-driven model with revenue of roughly 150 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (LGND). Raised about 2 billion dollars over time. B2B pharma brand with no consumer profile.

Nektar Therapeutics is a San Francisco biopharmaceutical company that develops immunology drugs, including rezpegaldesleukin for atopic dermatitis and alopecia areata, with an earlier focus on polymer-conjugate technology that produced partnered medicines. It has no big commercial products, earning mainly from collaborations. It has raised about 2.4 billion dollars, and is listed on Nasdaq (NKTR). Research-stage biotech with no consumer brand.

PTC Therapeutics is a South Plainfield, New Jersey biopharmaceutical company focused on rare disease medicines. Its products include Emflaza for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, Evrysdi (royalty from Roche) for spinal muscular atrophy, Translarna in Europe, Kebilidi for AADC deficiency and Sephience for PKU. Revenue is roughly 800 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (PTCT). Pharma brand with some patient community awareness, but little general consumer awareness.

Relay Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts clinical-stage precision-oncology company using its Dynamo platform, which combines computation and experiments, to design allosteric drugs. Programmes include RLY-2608 for breast cancer and vascular malformations. It has no marketed products and had an earlier partnership with Genentech. It has raised about 1.7 billion dollars and is listed on Nasdaq (RLAY). Research-stage biotech with no consumer brand.

ViiV Healthcare is a global specialist HIV company headquartered in London (with operations in Research Triangle Park, US), majority owned by GSK (about 78 percent) with Pfizer and Shionogi as minority shareholders. It sells antiretroviral medicines including Tivicay, Triumeq, Dovato, Juluca and the long-acting injectable Cabenuva and Apretude, to patients through health systems, with revenue of over 7 billion pounds. Healthcare brand, with HIV awareness campaigns but little consumer marketing.

WuXi AppTec is a Chinese contract research, development and manufacturing organisation based in Shanghai, providing outsourced chemistry, testing, cell and gene therapy services (WuXi Advanced Therapies sold in 2025) and small-molecule manufacturing, to pharmaceutical and biotech customers around the world. Revenue is about 40 billion yuan. It is listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange and Hong Kong (2359). B2B healthcare brand under US biosecurity scrutiny, with no consumer awareness.

Xenon Pharmaceuticals is a Burnaby, British Columbia neurology-focused biopharmaceutical company developing ion-channel modulators. Its lead candidate azetukalner (XEN1101), a Kv7 potassium channel opener, is in phase 3 trials for focal onset seizures and major depressive disorder, and it earlier partnered with Neurocrine Biosciences. It has no marketed products and has raised about 1.8 billion dollars from capital markets. It is listed on Nasdaq (XENE). Research-stage biotech with no consumer brand.

Zai Lab is a Shanghai biopharmaceutical company, with US offices, that licenses, develops and sells medicines in Greater China for cancer, autoimmune, infectious and neuroscience diseases. Its marketed products include Zejula, Qinlock, Nuzyra, Vyvgart and Tivdak, from partners such as GSK, argenx, Deciphera and Seagen. Revenue is around 400 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (ZLAB) and the Hong Kong exchange (9688). Pharma brand with no consumer marketing.

Genmab is a Danish biotechnology company headquartered in Copenhagen's Valby, founded in 1999, that develops antibody therapeutics for cancer and other diseases. Its products include Darzalex for multiple myeloma, marketed by Johnson & Johnson with Genmab receiving royalties, Kesimpta with Novartis, Tivdak and Epkinly with partners, and it acquired ProfoundBio in 2024 and Merus in 2025-2026. Customers are pharma partners and healthcare systems. Revenue is in the billions of dollars and it is listed on Nasdaq (GMAB) and Copenhagen. Low consumer brand awareness.

Eli Lilly is one of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies, headquartered in Indianapolis and founded in 1876. It develops and sells prescription medicines including the GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, Verzenio, Taltz, Jardiance with Boehringer Ingelheim, Humalog insulin and others, to health systems, pharmacies and patients in over 100 countries. Revenue exceeded $45 billion in 2024 and market capitalisation passed $700 billion in 2025. Listed on the NYSE under LLY. Major global corporate brand, though consumer promotion is limited by regulation.

Grifols is a Spanish healthcare company based in Sant Cugat del Valles near Barcelona, founded in 1909. It is one of the world's largest producers of plasma-derived medicines, operating hundreds of plasma donation centres mostly in the US, and also makes diagnostics, transfusion medicine products and hospital pharmacy supplies. Customers are hospitals, blood banks, health authorities and clinical labs, with sales in over 100 countries and revenue above EUR 6 billion. Listed on the Spanish stock exchange (GRF) with ADRs on Nasdaq (GRFS). B2B healthcare brand with low public awareness.

Labcorp is a US clinical laboratory and drug development group based in Burlington, North Carolina. Labcorp Diagnostics runs a large network of patient service centres and labs for physicians, hospitals and employers, while Labcorp Drug Development provides central lab and clinical trial services to pharma. It operates across the US, Europe and other markets, with revenue around $13 billion and more than 70,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE under LH. Well known among US patients and healthcare professionals, but primarily a B2B and healthcare brand.

Shanghai RAAS Blood Products is a Chinese plasma products company based in Shanghai, producing human albumin, immunoglobulins and coagulation factors from donated plasma collected at its plasma stations. Customers are Chinese hospitals and healthcare systems, and revenue comes from sales of plasma-derived therapies. Spanish group Grifols took a minority stake in the company around 2019, and Haier Group became its controlling shareholder in the 2020s. Listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. B2B healthcare, with low consumer brand awareness. Crunchbase shows CN 25 billion in funding as read.

about: Avidity Biosciences is a US biotechnology company based in San Diego, developing antibody oligonucleotide conjugates (AOCs) to treat muscle diseases such as myotonic dystrophy type 1, facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy and Duchenne. Its clinical programmes are del-desiran, del-brax and del-zota. It is listed on Nasdaq (RNA). In October 2025 Novartis agreed to acquire Avidity for about $12 billion. The Crunchbase description given refers to an unrelated consulting firm and appears to be a data error. Clinical-stage with no products on the market and no consumer visibility.

Baxter International is a US medical products company based in Deerfield, Illinois, founded in 1931. It makes hospital beds, infusion pumps, IV solutions, renal care and dialysis products, surgical and monitoring equipment and pharmaceuticals, and in 2021 acquired Hillrom. Customers are hospitals, dialysis clinics and healthcare systems in over 100 countries, with about 38,000 employees and revenue of roughly $10-11 billion. Kidney care was sold as Vantive to Carlyle in 2025. Listed on the NYSE under BAX. B2B healthcare brand with low consumer visibility.

Biohaven is a US biopharmaceutical company based in New Haven, Connecticut, developing treatments for neurological and neuropsychiatric diseases, including troriluzole for spinocerebellar ataxia, taldefgrobep alfa for spinal muscular atrophy and degraders for immune disorders. This is the 2022 spin-off of the earlier Biohaven Pharmaceuticals, whose migraine drug Nurtec ODT was bought by Pfizer for $11.6 billion in 2022. Customers will be neurologists and patients. It has no commercial revenue yet and is listed on the NYSE (BHVN). No consumer brand profile.

BioNTech is a German biotechnology company based in Mainz, founded in 2008 by Ugur Sahin and Ozlem Tureci. It co-developed the Comirnaty mRNA COVID-19 vaccine with Pfizer, and now focuses on cancer immunotherapies, mRNA, antibodies and cell therapies, acquiring CureVac in 2025 and licensing a PD-L1xVEGF antibody from Biotheus. Customers are governments, health systems and pharma partners, with revenue falling from the pandemic peak. About 7,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (BNTX). Highly recognised name from the pandemic, but little consumer advertising.

Braskem is Latin America's largest petrochemical company and a leading producer of biopolymers, headquartered in Sao Paulo. It makes polyethylene, polypropylene, PVC and green polyethylene from sugarcane ethanol, with plants in Brazil, the US, Mexico and Germany, and sells resins to plastics converters in packaging, automotive and construction. Revenue is around $15-20 billion. Controlled by Novonor (formerly Odebrecht) and Petrobras, and listed on B3 (BRKM5) and the NYSE (BAK). Pure B2B brand, though Braskem has appeared in Brazilian sports sponsorship.

Collegium Pharmaceutical is a US specialty pharma company based in Stoughton, Massachusetts, marketing pain medicines including Xtampza ER, Nucynta, Belbuca and Symproic, and acquired Ironshore, with a focus on abuse-deterrent formulations. Customers are pain specialists, pharmacies and payers in the United States. Revenue is around $700 million. Listed on Nasdaq under COLL. B2B pharma brand, with no consumer profile, and a restricted category for marketing.

Convatec is a UK medical products company based in London, developing and selling advanced wound dressings, ostomy and continence care products, critical care devices and infusion pumps for diabetes. Brands include Aquacel, Natura, Esteem and Flexi-Seal. Customers are hospitals, healthcare systems, clinicians and patients, with sales in over 100 countries, revenue of roughly $2.3 billion and about 10,000 employees. Founded in 1978 as part of Bristol-Myers Squibb, it was later owned by private equity and listed on the London Stock Exchange in 2016 (CTEC), a FTSE 100 member. Little consumer awareness.

Diversified Healthcare Trust is a US real estate investment trust headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts, managed by The RMR Group. It owns senior living communities, medical office buildings and life science properties across the United States, earning rental income and resident fees from operators and tenants. It was formed from the 2019 merger of Senior Housing Properties Trust and Government Properties Income Trust. Listed on Nasdaq under DHC. Balance-sheet heavy and financially stretched. B2B property investor with no consumer brand visibility.

Gevo is a US renewable fuels company based in Englewood, Colorado, developing sustainable aviation fuel and renewable gasoline from ethanol and isobutanol made from corn and other feedstocks. It is working on alcohol-to-jet production at its Net-Zero projects in North Dakota and South Dakota, and acquired the Red Trail Energy ethanol and carbon capture plant in 2024. Customers are airlines, fuel distributors and corporate buyers of low-carbon fuel. Listed on Nasdaq under GEVO, with limited revenue to date. Visible in clean energy circles, little consumer awareness.

Grail is a US healthcare company based in Menlo Park, California, that sells the Galleri blood test, a multi-cancer early detection screening test that looks for a cancer signal across more than 50 cancer types. Customers are consumers who pay via physicians, health systems and employers, with NHS England testing a large trial. It was founded by Illumina in 2016, spun out as a public company in June 2024, and trades on Nasdaq as GRAL. Still loss-making, with modest revenue. Reasonable public profile in health news.

Guardant Health is a US precision oncology company based in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2012. It sells blood-based tests including Guardant360 and Guardant Reveal for cancer therapy selection and recurrence monitoring, and Shield, an FDA-approved blood test for colorectal cancer screening. Customers are oncologists, hospitals, pharma companies and health systems. Revenue is above $700 million, and it is listed on Nasdaq under GH. B2B and healthcare provider brand, with limited but growing awareness among patients.

Immunovant is a clinical-stage US biopharmaceutical company, based in New York, developing antibodies that target the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) for autoimmune diseases such as myasthenia gravis, thyroid eye disease and Graves' disease. Pipeline assets include batoclimab and IMVT-1402. It is a majority-owned subsidiary of Roivant Sciences and is listed on Nasdaq under IMVT. It has no marketed products yet and earns no product revenue. B2B biotech with essentially no consumer brand awareness.

J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals is an Indian drug maker based in Mumbai that makes branded generics and contract manufactured formulations. Its brands include Rantac, Metrogyl, Cilacar and Nicardia, sold to Indian doctors and pharmacies, in addition to exports and CDMO work. In 2020 the investor KKR bought control, and in 2025 Torrent Pharmaceuticals agreed to acquire a controlling stake. Listed on the NSE and BSE under JBCHEPHARM. Familiar to Indian doctors and pharmacies, but moderate public brand awareness.

Kymera Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotech based in Watertown, Massachusetts, developing targeted protein degraders, small molecules that remove disease-causing proteins. Its lead programme KT-621 targets STAT6 for allergic and inflammatory diseases, and it has collaborations with Sanofi, Vertex and Gilead. Revenue comes from partnership payments rather than product sales. Listed on Nasdaq under KYMR. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Madrigal Pharmaceuticals is a US biopharmaceutical company based in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. Its product Rezdiffra (resmetirom), approved by the US FDA in March 2024 and in Europe in 2025, is the first approved medicine for non-alcoholic steatohepatitis with liver fibrosis (MASH). Customers are hepatologists, gastroenterologists, payers and patients. Sales are growing rapidly from launch. Listed on Nasdaq under MDGL. Small company with strong investor interest, low consumer awareness.

Nuvalent is a US clinical-stage oncology biotech based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing kinase inhibitors for lung cancer patients with ALK or ROS1 alterations, including zidesamtinib and neladalkib. The company is preparing to bring its first drugs to market following pivotal data and regulatory filings. It earns no product revenue yet and is funded through public offerings. Listed on Nasdaq under NUVL. Highly valued by investors but with no consumer brand profile.

Structure Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharma company with offices in South San Francisco and Shanghai, developing oral small-molecule drugs for obesity and metabolic diseases. Its lead candidate aleniglipron (GSBR-1290) is an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist in Phase 2 and later trials. It has no marketed products and is funded by equity raises, including a large 2025 offering. Listed on Nasdaq as GPCR via ADSs. B2B biotech with no consumer brand visibility.

Suzano is a Brazilian pulp and paper company headquartered in Sao Paulo, the world's largest producer of market eucalyptus pulp after its 2019 merger with Fibria. It also sells paper, packaging board and consumer tissue under brands such as Report and Neve, and moved into the international tissue business with Kimberly-Clark in 2025. Customers are tissue, paper and packaging manufacturers worldwide, mainly in China, Europe and North America. Controlled by the Feffer family and listed on B3 (SUZB3) and NYSE (SUZ). Largely B2B, with some Brazilian consumer brands.

Takeda is Japan's largest pharmaceutical company, headquartered in Tokyo and founded in 1781. It sells prescription medicines in gastroenterology (Entyvio), rare diseases, plasma-derived therapies, oncology and neuroscience (Vyvanse), after acquiring Shire in 2019, with operations in around 80 countries and revenue of more than 4 trillion yen. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and health systems. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (4502) and the NYSE (TAK). Well-known corporate brand but little consumer advertising.

Zealand Pharma is a Danish biotech based near Copenhagen (Soborg), listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen (ZEAL) and Nasdaq US, developing peptide-based medicines for obesity and metabolic disease: survodutide, partnered with Boehringer Ingelheim, and petrelintide, partnered with Roche since 2025. It also gets royalties from products like the rescue drug Zegalogue. Revenue is from milestones and royalties. Pharma B2B brand, known to investors and industry, with no consumer awareness, though obesity treatments have a high public profile.

Grunenthal is a family-owned German pharmaceutical group, based in Aachen, focused on pain, gout and inflammation, with products including Palexia (tapentadol), Nobligan (tramadol), Versatis and Qutenza, sold in Europe, Latin America and the US. It employs roughly 4,000 people and is owned by the Wirtz family. Revenue is from prescription drugs. Historically linked to thalidomide. Known mainly to physicians and pharmacists, with limited direct consumer awareness, although its brands are well recognised in some European markets.

Akeso is a Chinese biopharmaceutical company, listed in Hong Kong (9926), with a Zhongshan, Guangdong base, developing antibody drugs for cancer and immune disease, including cadonilimab (PD-1/CTLA-4) and ivonescimab (PD-1/VEGF), which it has licensed to Summit Therapeutics for markets outside China. Revenue is from product sales in China and licensing deals. Founded in 2012 by Michelle Xia. Known in oncology and investor circles, with no consumer awareness.
